Human results are inconsistent, and much of the positive signal comes from mouse and in-vitro work at doses hard to reach by drinking tea.
up.ref: Bond & Derbyshire 2019, Nutrients - Tea Compounds and the Gut Microbiome: Findings from Trials and Mechanistic Studies

up.note: IN VITRO, but human-derived and genus-level. A single dose of Psilocybe cubensis extract (35 mg/L) was fermented in the SHIME colonic model using faecal microbiota from people with severe anxiety. Bifidobacterium - the predominant genus in these samples - increased markedly after 20 h and again between 3 and 15 days; family-level Bifidobacteriaceae rose from 39.73% to 43.88% at 20 h and from 43.93% to 48.70% over 3-12 days. Critically for the cross-feeding question, SCFAs rose in parallel: acetic 2.26-fold, propionic 2.69-fold and BUTYRIC 2.21-fold at 20 h. Psilocybin and psilocin themselves were depleted during fermentation, i.e. the microbiota metabolises them. Two further metabolic effects: ammonia production fell 19-25% (ammonia is a gut irritant, so a reduction is favourable), while GABA levels DECREASED - counterintuitive for an anxiety-donor microbiota. Caveats: a fermentation vessel has no host, no absorption and no immune system; alpha-diversity fell slightly; and the authors are explicit that the cytokine and intestinal-barrier responses reflected a COMPLEX IMMUNOMODULATORY PATTERN rather than a uniform anti-inflammatory effect. They state plainly that these in vitro findings do not establish clinical benefit for intestinal or mental health.
up.ref: Salgaco et al. 2026, Drugs and Drug Candidates - SHIME colonic fermentation, faecal microbiota from individuals with severe anxiety, P. cubensis extract 35 mg/L (DOI 10.3390/ddc5030046)

up.note: Raised in a 6-week RCT of 89 older adults - but only in people who already had it. Non-responders were those with little Bifidobacterium at baseline; a 4-arm trial found 2'-FL alone gave inconsistent changes while plain oligofructose did better; a 2026 review of 12 infant RCTs found safety but 'limited evidence of benefits'; and in a fermenter 2'-FL alone did nothing until an HMO-utilising strain was added. It feeds what you have rather than establishing it. Species matter: B. infantis and B. bifidum use HMOs, B. adolescentis cannot.

up.note: LNT is the main component of the human-milk oligosaccharide pool, and lacto-N-biosidase (LNBase) is the key bifidobacterial enzyme that cleaves it into lacto-N-biose I plus lactose - the first step in using it at all. STRAIN-SPECIFIC, not a genus-wide given: LNBase activity is found in B. bifidum and only SOME B. longum subsp. longum strains, and the B. longum enzyme (LnbX/LnbY) is not even a homolog of B. bifidum's GH20 version. So an LNT supplement only benefits a Bifidobacterium population that happens to carry the enzyme.
up.ref: Sakurama et al. 2013, J Biol Chem - lacto-N-biosidase (LnbX/LnbY) from B. longum subsp. longum JCM1217; LNBase activity previously identified in B. bifidum and some B. longum strains (PMID 23843461)

up.note: LNB is the disaccharide LNT is cleaved into, and infant-gut-associated bifidobacteria have a dedicated GNB/LNB pathway for importing and phosphorylating it (N-acetylhexosamine 1-kinase, NahK). This is the intracellular half of HMO use: LNBase releases LNB outside the cell, this pathway consumes it. Described for infant-gut bifidobacteria specifically, so do not assume it of every adult-gut Bifidobacterium.
up.ref: Sakurama/Nishimoto et al. 2015, Biochim Biophys Acta - N-acetylhexosamine 1-kinase (NahK) structures; infant-gut bifidobacteria use a dedicated GNB/LNB pathway for these two disaccharides (PMID 25644306)

up.note: GNB enters the SAME bifidobacterial pathway as LNB (that is why it is called the GNB/LNB pathway) - one transport and phosphorylation route serving a milk-derived sugar and a host-mucin-derived one. This is the mechanism behind bifidobacteria persisting after weaning: when milk oligosaccharides stop arriving, host mucin O-glycans supply the same substrate class.
up.ref: Sakurama/Nishimoto et al. 2015, Biochim Biophys Acta - N-acetylhexosamine 1-kinase (NahK) structures; infant-gut bifidobacteria use a dedicated GNB/LNB pathway for these two disaccharides (PMID 25644306)

up.note: The bifidogenic effect is the best-replicated HMO result in adults: a 100-person RCT (relative abundance of Bifidobacterium rose substantially), a SHIME fermentation model where 2'FL, LNnT and their mix all raised bifidobacteria with a rise in SCFAs, and a randomised IBS trial where a 2'FL/LNnT mix raised fecal bifidobacteria without worsening overall GI symptoms. LNnT has more human data behind it than LNT, LNB and GNB combined - and note it is a DIFFERENT molecule from LNT (beta1-4 vs beta1-3 linkage, different bacterial enzymes). ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT: the trial gave 2'FL and LNnT alone and in mixes at several doses and reports the pooled HMO effect, so the split between the two molecules is not clean.
up.ref: Elison et al. 2016, Br J Nutr - randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 100 healthy adults, 2'FL and/or LNnT up to 20 g/day for 2 weeks (PMID 27719686); Suligoj et al. 2020, Nutrients - SHIME (PMID 32933181); Iribarren et al. 2020, Neurogastroenterol Motil - randomised IBS trial, 2'FL/LNnT (PMID 32536023)

both.note: Context-dependent, so 'both'. The mechanism explains the split: E. coli and B. bifidum cooperatively degrade 2'-FL (E. coli supplies cysteine, then feeds on the freed sugars, PMID 42020426), so 2'-FL can partly FEED E. coli in a healthy gut while the SCFA shift crowds it out under pathogen challenge. Kept the existing Nat Commun 'down' citation and added both sides rather than picking one. (both) | Ulcerative colitis: Main Bacteroidaceae-family species significantly reduced in UC stool. Genuine contradiction: a separate primary study (n=48 UC/48 controls) found Bacteroides directly proportional to disease severity — i.e. elevated, not reduced — and higher baseline Bacteroides associated with worse relapse outcomes (PMID 36344781). Kept the existing Polish-cohort 'down' citation and added both sides. (both)

up.note: INDIRECT / cross-fed, not a direct effect. Bifidobacterium infantis metabolises 2'-FL and releases acetate, lactate and 1,2-propanediol; E. hallii consumes those to produce butyrate. The syntrophy is structure- and strain-specific — it depends on which fucosylated HMO and which B. infantis strain is present. Shown in in-vitro co-culture and a modelled microbiome, not measured in a human supplementation trial. Notably, one study found the B. adolescentis to A. hallii to butyrate link only in ADULTS, so this cross-feeding route may matter more in adults than infants. EVIDENCE TIER CORRECTED to in-vitro: B. infantis/E. hallii syntrophy is an in-vitro co-culture study (PMID 36938958), not a human measurement — so 'Human studies only' now hides it.
up.ref: Mol Nutr Food Res 2023 — B. infantis/E. hallii syntrophy on 2'FL (PMID 36938958)

up.note: The only species showing consensus enrichment across chronic insomnia cohorts; independently confirmed as significantly increased in a separate 14-study meta-analysis.

up.note: FROM CROSS-FEEDING - inferred, not measured for this entry. Bifidobacterium is up here, and Bifidobacterium feeds Eubacterium hallii (acetate, lactate, 1,2-propanediol -> butyrate), so Eubacterium hallii is expected to follow. Same direction as the demonstrated cross-feed. The underlying feeding relationship is real (in-vitro-coculture); its presence in THIS condition/symptom is an inference. Source edge: cf_infantis_ehallii. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: 2 separate feeding routes imply the same direction here - also Akkermansia -> Eubacterium hallii (mucus-derived oligosaccharides, acetate, 1,2-propanediol, in-vitro-coculture, cf_akkermansia_eubacterium_hall).

up.note: INDIRECT / cross-fed, not a direct effect. 2'-FL is not consumed by F. prausnitzii itself — Bifidobacterium bifidum degrades the HMO and releases the constituent sugars plus acetate and lactate, which F. prausnitzii then converts to butyrate. Demonstrated in in-vitro co-culture, so this is a mechanism established in the lab rather than a measured outcome in people; the human 2'-FL RCTs in this app only reported Bifidobacterium itself. Worth noting the cross-feeding chain is the reason a bifidogenic prebiotic can raise butyrate without directly feeding any butyrate producer. DOSE OF REALISM from the same head-to-head study: F. prausnitzii in monoculture reached a LOWER cell density on the HMOs than on glucose, and in coculture with B. longum subsp. infantis it was 6'-sialyllactose rather than 2'-FL that promoted growth. The cross-feeding route is real but 2'-FL is not obviously the best substrate for driving it (PMID 33193162).
up.ref: Microorganisms 2025 — B. bifidum/F. prausnitzii co-culture (PMID 40732214); Front Microbiol 2020, HMO growth panel + coculture (PMID 33193162)

up.note: FROM CROSS-FEEDING - inferred, not measured for this entry. Bifidobacterium is up here, and Bifidobacterium feeds Faecalibacterium prausnitzii (constituent sugars from HMO degradation, acetate, lactate -> butyrate), so Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is expected to follow. Same direction as the demonstrated cross-feed. The underlying feeding relationship is real (in-vitro-coculture); its presence in THIS condition/symptom is an inference.
